title: WT Control Series Equivalence
text:
Two wild-type/WT datasets were collected, one as part of (i) the solvent-exchange experiment series, and (ii) for the mutant experiment series.
Our question can be phrased as:

Are there systematic differences between these two WT control series that would prevent us pooling the data from the two series in any analysis?

Essentially, the question asks “can we ascribe a plausible non-zero difference in WT maximum amplitude or decay rate to the effect of a Series/batch parameter for the experiment, conditioned on LPR (which we anticipate affects both measurements)?”
Neither answer, yes or no, would prevent downstream statistical analysis, would inform how we use the control data. The two WT datasets will always be reasonable controls for their corresponding experimental series, but if there is no effect ascribable to Series, we have some justification for pooling the data. If there is a discernible effect due to Series we can incorporate Series as an explanatory variable and estimate its effect separately from that of the treatments we are interested in, should we require to pool the data.


We process the dfm_wt_1 and dfm_wt_2 (WT control) dataframes, to add a column indicating series, and unify the columns (Table 1).

Show the code
# Use helper script to load dataframes
source("assets/r/load_dataframes.R")
dfms <- load_dataframes()

dfm1 <- dfms$dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::mutate(Series = "Series 2") |>
  dplyr::filter(Condition == "H2O") |>
  dplyr::filter(LPR != "LPR50") |>
  dplyr::select(Series, LPR, Max_Amplitude, Decay_Rate)

dfm2 <- dfms$dfm_wt_2 |> dplyr::mutate(Series = "Series 1") |>
  dplyr::filter(LPR != "LPR50") |>
  dplyr::select(Series, LPR, Max_Amplitude, Decay_Rate)

dfm_comp <- rbind(dfm1, dfm2)

# Show interactive tables of data
DT::datatable(dfm_comp)




Table 1: Measurements for WT across two series. Values are measured at two values of LPR: LPR5 and LPR10











We visualise the distributions of datapoints between series, for each LPR value (Figure 1).


Show the code
p1_amp <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_comp, ggplot2::aes(x=Series, y=Max_Amplitude, color=Series)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~LPR) +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Maximum amplitude (nA)", x="") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() + 
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))

# Visualise datasets as box/whisker with superimposed datapoints
p1_k <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_comp, ggplot2::aes(x=Series, y=Decay_Rate, color=Series)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~LPR) +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Decay rate constant k (/s)", x="") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() + 
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))

ggpubr::ggarrange(p1_amp, p1_k)








Figure 1: WT measurements across LPR5 and LPR10 for two batches/series





Visually we might expect from Figure 1 that the means of maximum amplitude between Series do not differ. We might have similar expectations for decay rate at LPR10, though not at LPR5.
An apparent difference in decay rate at LPR5 may induce an interaction effect in any linear model fit. There also appears, visually, to be a difference in variance (heteroscedasticity) between the two series: Series 2 looks to have greater variance than Series 1.



Our central question is whether there is a nonzero effect on maximum amplitude or decay rate constant in WT, conditioned on LPR value, due to the choice of Series



We address the question using a linear model, treating LPR and Series as main effects. As we suspect from Figure 1 that the effects of Series may not be independent of LPR, we use a linear model with interactions.

Show the code
model1_amp_lm <- lm(Max_Amplitude ~ LPR * Series, data=dfm_comp)
model1_k_lm <- lm(Decay_Rate ~ LPR * Series, data=dfm_comp)

gtsummary::tbl_regression(model1_amp_lm)
gtsummary::tbl_regression(model1_k_lm)

These model results (Table 2) indicate that there is a reduction of maximum amplitude (-0.93nA, 95%CI[-1.1, -0.73]) and decay rate constant (-11/s, 95%CI[-20, -2.9]) on increasing LPR from LPR5 to LPR10.
The model fit indicates no effect on maximum amplitude due to the Series (-0.20nA [-0.43, -0.02]). However, Series does appear to be associated with a difference in decay rate constant (15/s, 95%CI[5.6, 25]), at a similar magnitude to the effect of increasing LPR.
There is, for both models, no strong evidence of an interaction effect due to the way Series interacts with LPR.



We have so far only assumed that our data are suitable for linear modelling. We check whether the data meet requirements in Figure 2.

Show the code

While both models are acceptably linear with a normal distribution of residuals (Figure 2), there is a suggestion of heteroscedasticity, particularly for decay rate data (though the curve fit is suspect). To be cautious we therefore calculate heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors, and recalculate effect sizes for the model parameters in Table 3.

title: Supplementary Online Information for Henderson et al. (2026)
text:
This site is provided to enable reproduction and independent exploration of the statistical analyses reported in Henderson et al. (2026).
These pages describe linear regression modelling for the manuscript “A bacterial Rhesus transporter retunes a structurally conserved ammonium pore into a reversible nitrogen valve.” We analyse this data to establish evidence in support of answers to the following key questions:

Whether the two WT control datasets from solvent-exchange and variant comparison can be pooled.
Whether, in the H2O condition, there are effects on maximum amplitude or decay rate constant due to lipid-protein ratio or D162A substitution.
Whether there are effects on maximum amplitude or decay rate constant due to H170 substitution.

title: Figure 1: WT maximum amplitudes and decay rate constants
text: Manuscript figure 1 uses three subfigures to show WT maximum amplitude and decay rate constant variation over LPR5, LPR10, and LPR50 for the H2O condition (figure 1B); WT maximum amplitude variation over LPR5 and LPR10 for H2O, D2O, and H2O>D2O conditions (figure 1D); and WT maximum amplitude and decay rate constant variation over LPR5, LPR10, and LPR50 for D2O experiments (figure 1F).

title: Figure 1: WT maximum amplitudes and decay rate constants
text:
The Dataset
We begin with the WT raw data for figure 1.csv dataset (Table 1).


Show the code
# Use helper script to load dataframes
source("assets/r/load_dataframes.R")
dfms <- load_dataframes()
dfm_wt_1 <- dfms$dfm_wt_1

# Show interactive tables of data
DT::datatable(dfm_wt_1)




Table 1: Measurements for WT across H2O, D2O and D2O>H2O conditions for three values of LPR: LPR5, LPR10 and LPR50










We visualise the datasets in the style of figure 1 in Figure 1.


Show the code
p1b_amp <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "H2O"), 
                           ggplot2::aes(x=LPR, y=Max_Amplitude, color=LPR)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Maximum amplitude (nA)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

p1b_k <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "H2O"), 
                         ggplot2::aes(x=LPR, y=Decay_Rate, color=LPR)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Decay rate constant k (/s)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

p1d_amp <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(LPR %in% c("LPR5", "LPR10")), 
                           ggplot2::aes(x=Condition, y=Max_Amplitude, color=Condition)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Maximum amplitude (nA)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~LPR)

p1d_k <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(LPR %in% c("LPR5", "LPR10")), 
                         ggplot2::aes(x=Condition, y=Decay_Rate, color=Condition)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Decay rate constant k (/s)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~LPR)

p1f_amp <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "D2O"), 
                           ggplot2::aes(x=LPR, y=Max_Amplitude, color=LPR)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Maximum amplitude (nA)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

p1f_k <- ggplot2::ggplot(dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "D2O"), 
                         ggplot2::aes(x=LPR, y=Decay_Rate, color=LPR)) +
  ggplot2::geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_jitter() +
  ggplot2::labs(y="Decay rate constant k (/s)") +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()

ggpubr::ggarrange(p1b_amp, p1b_k, p1d_amp, p1d_k, p1f_amp, p1f_k,
                  ncol=2, nrow=3,
                  labels=c("B", "", "D", "", "F", ""),
                  legend="none")








Figure 1: WT measurements across three LPRs and three experimental conditions, representing figures 1B, 1D, and 1F from the draft manuscript.






The Questions
We have multiple questions for this dataset. Within each of the six plots we wish to present the effects of the parameters plotted along the x-axis, for each measurement.


The Models
We address these questions using a separate linear model for each set of figure data. For figures 1B and 1F we treat maximum amplitude and decay rate constant as dependent variables, and fit these to the LPR explanatory variable (Value ~ LPR). For figure 1D we proceed in a similar way, but separately fit maximum amplitude values for LPR5 and LPR10 to the Condition explanatory variable (Max_Amplitude ~ Condition).

Show the code
model1b_amp_lm <- lm(Max_Amplitude ~ LPR, data=dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "H2O"))
model1b_k_lm <- lm(Decay_Rate ~ LPR, data=dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "H2O"))

model1d_lpr5_lm <- lm(Max_Amplitude ~ Condition, data=dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(LPR == "LPR5"))
model1d_lpr10_lm <- lm(Max_Amplitude ~ Condition, data=dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(LPR == "LPR10"))

model1f_amp_lm <- lm(Max_Amplitude ~ LPR, data=dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "D2O"))
model1f_k_lm <- lm(Decay_Rate ~ LPR, data=dfm_wt_1 |> dplyr::filter(Condition == "D2O"))

performance::check_model(model1b_amp_lm, size_title=6)
performance::check_model(model1b_k_lm, size_title=6)
performance::check_model(model1d_lpr5_lm, size_title=6)
performance::check_model(model1d_lpr10_lm, size_title=6)
performance::check_model(model1f_amp_lm, size_title=6)
performance::check_model(model1f_k_lm, size_title=6)

Figure 2: Diagnostic plots for linear model fits of Value ~ LPR and Max_amplitude ~ Condition



There are no obvious departures from assumptions in Figure 2, although some of the diagnostic plots do have odd spline fits. We extract the contrasts in Table 2.

We can plot these differences in the style of the manuscript as in Figure 3


Show the code
# Get p-values, accounting for heteroscedasticity and multiple testing
# Also generate group1 and group2 columns
EMM_amp_b <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model1b_amp_lm, ~ LPR),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=3) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

EMM_k_b <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model1b_k_lm, ~ LPR),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=90) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

EMM_lpr5_d <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model1d_lpr5_lm, ~ Condition),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=3) |>
  rstatix::add_significance() |>
  dplyr::mutate(LPR="LPR5")

EMM_lpr10_d <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model1d_lpr10_lm, ~ Condition),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=3) |>
  rstatix::add_significance() |>
  dplyr::mutate(LPR="LPR10")

EMM_d <- rbind(EMM_lpr5_d, EMM_lpr10_d)
EMM_d$LPR <- factor(EMM_d$LPR, levels=c("LPR5", "LPR10"))

EMM_amp_f <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model1f_amp_lm, ~ LPR),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=3) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

EMM_k_f <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans::emmeans(model1f_k_lm, ~ LPR),
                               adjust="sidak")) |>
  tidyr::separate(contrast, into=c("group1", "group2"), sep=" - ") |>
  dplyr::mutate(y.position=90) |>
  rstatix::add_significance()

p1b_amp_annot <- p1b_amp +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_amp_b,
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}",
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)

p1b_k_annot <- p1b_k +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_k_b, 
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}", 
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)

p1d_annot <- p1d_amp +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_d,
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}",
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)

p1f_amp_annot <- p1f_amp +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_amp_f,
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}",
                             size=3, step.increase=0.1)

p1f_k_annot <- p1f_k +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(EMM_k_f, 
                             label="p = {scales::pvalue(p.value)}",

ggpubr::ggarrange(p1b_amp_annot, p1b_k_annot, p1d_annot,
